method.pass_1: Reference, Greek text unit, speaker boundary, quote type, and literal English checked against the Faithlife/SBLGNT raw text.
method.pass_2: Scene, chronology, Gospel layer, parallels, literary dependence, and visual implication checked independently after pass 1.

cards.greek: φωνὴ βοῶντος ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ· Ἑτοιμάσατε τὴν ὁδὸν κυρίου, εὐθείας ποιεῖτε τὰς τρίβους αὐτοῦ
cards.literal_english: A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.
cards.display_quote: Prepare the way of the Lord.
cards.speaker: Narrator citing Scripture
cards.historical_status: Earliest extant Gospel opening; later Gospel parallels are not four independent votes.

cards.greek: ἐγένετο Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτίζων ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ κηρύσσων βάπτισμα μετανοίας εἰς ἄφεσιν ἁμαρτιῶν
cards.literal_english: John came, baptizing in the wilderness and proclaiming a baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
cards.display_quote: John came, baptizing in the wilderness.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Earliest extant narrative introduction of John the Baptist.

cards.greek: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία χώρα καὶ οἱ Ἱεροσολυμῖται πάντες, καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν
cards.literal_english: All the Judean country and all the people of Jerusalem were going out to him and were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
cards.display_quote: They were baptized by him in the Jordan.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Markan crowd summary; not a census claim.

cards.greek: καὶ ἦν ὁ Ἰωάννης ἐνδεδυμένος τρίχας καμήλου καὶ ζώνην δερματίνην περὶ τὴν ὀσφὺν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔσθων ἀκρίδας καὶ μέλι ἄγριον
cards.literal_english: John was clothed with camel hair and a leather belt around his waist, and was eating locusts and wild honey.
cards.display_quote: He was clothed with camel hair and a leather belt.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Earliest extant description; later echoed by Matthew.

cards.greek: Ἔρχεται ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου ὀπίσω μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς κύψας λῦσαι τὸν ἱμάντα τῶν ὑποδημάτων αὐτοῦ
cards.literal_english: The stronger one than I comes after me, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.
cards.display_quote: The stronger one than I comes after me.
cards.speaker: John the Baptist
cards.historical_status: Multiple-Gospel motif with literary dependence and wording differences.

cards.greek: ἐγὼ ἐβάπτισα ὑμᾶς ὕδατι, αὐτὸς δὲ βαπτίσει ὑμᾶς ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ
cards.literal_english: I baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with holy spirit.
cards.display_quote: I baptized you with water; he will baptize you with holy spirit.
cards.speaker: John the Baptist
cards.historical_status: Early shared water/spirit contrast; Matthew and Luke add fire.

cards.greek: ἦλθεν Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲτ τῆς Γαλιλαίας
cards.literal_english: Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee.
cards.display_quote: Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Opening movement of the earliest extant baptism narrative.

cards.greek: καὶ ἐβαπτίσθη εἰς τὸν Ἰορδάνην ὑπὸ Ἰωάννου
cards.literal_english: And he was baptized in the Jordan by John.
cards.display_quote: He was baptized in the Jordan by John.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Mark explicitly names John as baptizer; Luke leaves the baptizer unnamed in its scene and John reframes the event as witness.

cards.greek: καὶ εὐθὺς ἀναβαίνων ἐκ τοῦ ὕδατος εἶδεν σχιζομένους τοὺς οὐρανούς
cards.literal_english: Immediately, coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens being torn apart.
cards.display_quote: He saw the heavens being torn apart.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Markan tearing-open image; later Synoptic wording is less abrupt.

cards.greek: Σὺ εἶ ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν σοὶ εὐδόκησα
cards.literal_english: You are my beloved Son; in you I delighted.
cards.display_quote: You are my beloved Son; in you I delighted.
cards.speaker: Heavenly voice within narration
cards.historical_status: Mark addresses Jesus directly; Matthew changes the public grammatical framing. Luke 3:22 also has an important alternative ancient reading.

cards.greek: Καὶ μετὰ τὸ παραδοθῆναι τὸν Ἰωάννην ἦλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν κηρύσσων τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ θεοῦ
cards.literal_english: After John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God.
cards.display_quote: After John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Markan handover hinge. The Greek says handed over, not merely absent.

cards.greek: Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν τὴν γυναῖκα τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου
cards.literal_english: It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.
cards.display_quote: It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.
cards.speaker: John the Baptist
cards.historical_status: Earliest extant Gospel conflict account; Josephus gives a different political-crowd emphasis.

cards.greek: καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦλθον καὶ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔθηκαν αὐτὸ ἐν μνημείῳ
cards.literal_english: When his disciples heard, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb.
cards.display_quote: They took his body and placed it in a tomb.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Earliest extant Gospel burial close; visualize without gore. Josephus independently places John's imprisonment and death at Machaerus but explains Herod's motive differently.

cards.greek: Μετανοεῖτε· ἤγγικεν γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν
cards.literal_english: Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.
cards.display_quote: Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has drawn near.
cards.speaker: John the Baptist
cards.historical_status: Matthean opening formulation; not an independent eyewitness vote from Mark.

cards.greek: τότε ἐξεπορεύετο πρὸς αὐτὸν Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ πᾶσα ἡ Ἰουδαία καὶ πᾶσα ἡ περίχωρος τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ ἐβαπτίζοντο ἐν τῷ Ἰορδάνῃ ποταμῷ ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ ἐξομολογούμενοι τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν
cards.literal_english: Then Jerusalem, all Judea, and all the region around the Jordan were going out to him, and they were baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
cards.display_quote: They were baptized by him in the Jordan.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Matthew reuses and reshapes the earlier Markan crowd-and-baptism summary; it is not a second independent eyewitness vote.

cards.greek: Γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν, τίς ὑπέδειξεν ὑμῖν φυγεῖν ἀπὸ τῆς μελλούσης ὀργῆς;
cards.literal_english: Offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
cards.display_quote: Offspring of vipers—who warned you to flee?
cards.speaker: John the Baptist
cards.historical_status: Matthew–Luke double tradition, often associated with the hypothetical Q source; Q is a scholarly reconstruction, not a recovered manuscript.

cards.greek: ποιήσατε οὖν καρπὸν ἄξιον τῆς μετανοίας· ἤδη δὲ ἡ ἀξίνη πρὸς τὴν ῥίζαν τῶν δένδρων κεῖται· πᾶν οὖν δένδρον μὴ ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλὸν ἐκκόπτεται καὶ εἰς πῦρ βάλλεται
cards.literal_english: Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance. Already the axe lies at the root of the trees; every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into fire.
cards.display_quote: Produce fruit worthy of repentance.
cards.speaker: John the Baptist
cards.historical_status: Matthew–Luke double tradition; the shared wording does not make the two texts fully independent witnesses.

cards.greek: Ἐγὼ μὲν ὑμᾶς βαπτίζω ἐν ὕδατι εἰς μετάνοιαν· ὁ δὲ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἰσχυρότερός μού ἐστιν, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς τὰ ὑποδήματα βαστάσαι· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί
cards.literal_english: I baptize you in water for repentance; but the one coming after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you in holy spirit and fire.
cards.display_quote: He will baptize you in holy spirit and fire.
cards.speaker: John the Baptist
cards.historical_status: The stronger-one and water/spirit contrast is multiply preserved; Matthew and Luke add fire to Mark's wording.

cards.greek: οὗ τὸ πτύον ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ συνάξει τὸν σῖτον αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ
cards.literal_english: His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will thoroughly clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.
cards.display_quote: His winnowing fork is in his hand.
cards.speaker: John the Baptist
cards.historical_status: Matthew–Luke double tradition preserving an apocalyptic judgment image; absent from Mark's surviving account.

cards.greek: Τότε παραγίνεται ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀπὸ τῆς Γαλιλαίας ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰορδάνην πρὸς τὸν Ἰωάννην τοῦ βαπτισθῆναι ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ
cards.literal_english: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.
cards.display_quote: Jesus came to John to be baptized by him.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Matthew retains Mark's explicit John-to-Jesus baptism link before adding an explanatory dialogue.

cards.greek: Ἐγὼ χρείαν ἔχω ὑπὸ σοῦ βαπτισθῆναι, καὶ σὺ ἔρχῃ πρός με;
cards.literal_english: I have need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?
cards.display_quote: I need to be baptized by you—and you come to me?
cards.speaker: John the Baptist
cards.historical_status: Matthean redaction: John's objection is absent from the earlier Markan account and from Luke's baptism scene.

cards.greek: Ἄφες ἄρτι, οὕτως γὰρ πρέπον ἐστὶν ἡμῖν πληρῶσαι πᾶσαν δικαιοσύνην
cards.literal_english: Allow it now, for in this way it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness.
cards.display_quote: Allow it now—to fulfill all righteousness.
cards.speaker: Jesus
cards.historical_status: Matthean redaction: Jesus' answer is absent from Mark and is not independently attested in the other Gospels.

cards.greek: Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱός μου ὁ ἀγαπητός, ἐν ᾧ εὐδόκησα
cards.literal_english: This is my beloved Son, in whom I delighted.
cards.display_quote: This is my beloved Son; in him I delighted.
cards.speaker: Heavenly voice within narration
cards.historical_status: Matthew changes Mark's direct second-person address ('You are') into a public third-person declaration ('This is').

cards.greek: Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ βλέπετε· τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν καὶ χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν, λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται καὶ κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, καὶ νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται καὶ πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται
cards.literal_english: Go and report to John what you hear and see: blind people see again and lame people walk, lepers are cleansed and deaf people hear, and dead people are raised and poor people receive good news.
cards.display_quote: Report to John what you hear and see.
cards.speaker: Jesus
cards.historical_status: Matthew–Luke double tradition: Jesus answers John's inquiry by pointing to deeds rather than supplying a simple title.

cards.greek: ἡ γυνή σου Ἐλισάβετ γεννήσει υἱόν σοι
cards.literal_english: Your wife Elizabeth will bear a son for you.
cards.speaker: Angelic messenger within narration
cards.historical_status: Luke-only infancy tradition; not independently attested by the other Gospels or Josephus.

cards.greek: οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖνος τὸ φῶς, ἀλλʼ ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός
cards.literal_english: He was not the light, but came to testify about the light.
cards.speaker: Narrator
cards.historical_status: Johannine theological frame; the lamp scene is a labeled visual metaphor, not a narrated event.
